questions.q: What is a key flexfield, in plain terms?
options: Oracle's underlying mechanism for building a structure out of independently-defined segments that combine into one composite key
A type of legal reporting unit
A reference data determinant
A conversion rate type used for currency translation
questions.explain: A key flexfield is the technical mechanism chart of accounts structures (via the Accounting Flexfield) are built on.

questions.q: In the freeze-and-deploy sequence, what happens immediately after defining segments and before deploying the structure?
options: Assigning business units
Freezing the structure definition
Opening the first accounting period
Running cross-validation rules
questions.explain: The sequence runs: define segments, freeze the structure definition, then deploy the structure.

questions.q: What is required before a structure instance can actually be used by a ledger?
options: The instance must be converted into a reference data set
Only the chart of accounts structure needs deployment; instances need nothing further
Each structure instance must also be frozen and deployed, after value sets are assigned to it
A legal entity must be deleted first
questions.explain: Both the structure itself and each structure instance built on it go through their own freeze-and-deploy cycle.

questions.q: What kinds of changes to a chart of accounts structure typically require redeployment and can seriously affect reporting and historical data?
options: Renaming a business unit
Updating a daily currency rate
Changing a report's font color
Removing a segment, changing segment widths, or reordering segments
questions.explain: Structural changes like removing, resizing, or reordering segments are disruptive after deployment, unlike some limited additions.

questions.q: Why is freezing and deploying the chart of accounts structure often treated as a formally reviewed milestone in real implementations?
options: Because it has no real consequences and is purely procedural
Because undoing or changing it afterward can be highly disruptive to reporting, transactions, and historical data
Because it must be repeated every accounting period
Because only Oracle support can perform this step
questions.explain: Given how disruptive a reversal would be, deployment is typically treated as a significant, sign-off-worthy milestone on real projects.
